mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at +16–17% above baseline over the past four weeks, indicating sustained lockdown compliance. This persistent elevation in home-based activity directly suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility by reducing opportunity for out-of-home consumption, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +16.0 to +17.1 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28-day mean, or RESIDENTIAL drops below +10% while RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines.

mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility has remained depressed at −54 to −60% for four consecutive weeks, signaling sustained avoidance of public transportation. This persistent transit collapse prevents commuters from reaching retail districts, mechanically reducing RETAIL_REC footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranges from −54.3 to −60.1 across four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility recovers to above −40% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously declines, or RETAIL_REC rises despite TRANSIT remaining below −50%.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has declined from −25.7% (t-3w) to −27.3% (t-0w), indicating tightening constraints on essential shopping. When essential-goods mobility contracts, consumers defer discretionary retail visits, producing a negative feedback loop that suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below −27% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at −27.3% in t-0w, lowest in series
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM recovers above −20% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not decline, or RETAIL_REC rises despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining below −27%.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has deteriorated from −41.6% (t-3w) to −47.9% (t-1w), then partially recovered to −38.0% (t-0w). This week-to-week volatility in outdoor recreation signals shifting behavioral constraints. When parks mobility recovers, consumers substitute outdoor for indoor retail, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered 9.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to rise above −35% and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases, or PARKS declines below −45% while RETAIL_REC falls.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has remained stable at −46.9 to −52.7% across four weeks, indicating sustained remote-work adoption. When combined with elevated residential mobility (+16–17%), this dual signal reveals a structural shift away from commuting and urban center visitation, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL show inverse relationship across all weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers above −40% and RESIDENTIAL drops below +12% simultaneously, and RETAIL_REC increases; or either series reverses trend without corresponding RETAIL_REC decline.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation mobility has contracted to −60.1% (t-0w), the highest (least negative) value in the four-week window. This marginal improvement signals early policy relaxation or consumer adaptation. If this recovery momentum continues, RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks as restrictions ease further.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises above −60% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines below −62% in the next four weeks, or remains flat at −60% ± 2 points despite policy announcements of further reopening.

mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility (−55.9%) and workplace mobility (−47.1%) are both severely depressed at t-0w, but transit is proportionally more constrained. If transit recovers faster than workplaces over the next two weeks, commuters will regain access to retail districts, driving RETAIL_REC upward. This interaction between transport access and employment location determines retail footfall.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 10 percentage points while WORKPLACES remains flat or declines
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at −55.9%, WORKPLACES at −47.1% at t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above −40% but WORKPLACES remains below −50%, and RETAIL_REC does not increase; or both series remain flat and RETAIL_REC declines.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility (−27.3%) and parks mobility (−38.0%) are both near their four-week lows at t-0w. When essential and recreational mobility are simultaneously constrained, consumers lack both functional and hedonic reasons to visit retail districts. This dual suppression will keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks unless both categories recover together.
candidate_trigger: both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS remain below their t-3w levels for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at −27.3%, PARKS at −38.0% at t-0w
failure_condition: Either GROCERY_PHARM or PARKS recovers above −20% while the other remains depressed, and RETAIL_REC increases; or both recover but RETAIL_REC declines.
